title: Hazel and the Choir
premise: Jonah Nystrom, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the ivory he carves, keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things — borrowed years, traded names, weather sold by the season. When tonight's date surfaces in a century-old book of prophecies, Jonah is pulled into a broken covenant between the human realm and the Choir, the singing dead who once kept winter gentle. Hunted by guild enforcers and courted by the dead alike, Jonah must reforge the covenant with Hazel, a prophecy-keeper's daughter whose voice can bind what law cannot. The price of survival is steep: someone must remain on the other side as the covenant's living anchor, and in the end Jonah chooses to stay, sending Hazel home to carry their story into spring.
about_author: P. M. Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild ledgers from coastal trading towns before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about bargains, borders, and the people who keep the books when the magic goes wrong.

chapters.title: The Ledger Opens Itself
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. In the Vellum Guild's counting house, Jonah records an impossible sale — a summer, lightly used — when a prophecy ledger flips to today's date and writes back. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the moment routine becomes fate, and the first whisper of the Choir bleeds through the page.

chapters.title: A Girl with Her Mother's Voice
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. Hazel arrives at the guild demanding her missing mother's debts be honored, carrying half a prophecy written in a hand she recognizes as her own future one. She and Jonah discover their names share a line. The beat is wary alliance — two strangers bound by ink neither chose.

chapters.title: What the Dead Charge
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Guided by a carved bone that hums, Jonah enters the border-market where the Choir trades memories for warmth. He learns the covenant broke when the guild stopped paying its tithe of songs. The beat is vertigo: his employer's honest ledgers are built on theft from the dead.

chapters.title: Enforcers at the Door
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. Guild enforcers raid the counting house to seize the prophecy ledger; Hazel hides inside its margins, literally, as the book swallows her. She glimpses her mother alive on the far side. The beat is betrayal sharpening into resolve — the law will not save them, so they'll go around it.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falling
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Frost creeps inland as the unbound Choir grieves without ritual; villages trade away their names just to stay warm. Jonah carves a listening-bone from his own childhood relic and hears his grandmother among the dead. The beat is grief turned to purpose: this winter has a face, and it knows him.

chapters.title: Terms of Reforging
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. In the border-market, Hazel negotiates with the Choir's eldest singer: the covenant can be remade if a living voice anchors it willingly — no coercion, no trickery, which is exactly why the guild never managed it. The beat is terrible clarity: justice exists here, but it prices everything honestly.

chapters.title: The Guild's Last Entry
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Jonah confronts the guildmaster, who reveals the tithe was ended deliberately to hoard the Choir's power for one family's immortality. Jonah burns his own employment contract in the ledger fire. The beat is severance: choosing the dead's justice over the living's law, knowing there's no going back.

chapters.title: Sung Across the Ice
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. At the frozen border, Hazel sings the old covenant while enforcers and winter itself close in; Jonah carves anchor-runes into his own bones so the binding will hold. The climax lands mid-song: the covenant takes root, but the anchor must stay. The beat is sacrifice offered freely.

chapters.title: One Stays, One Goes
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. The door holds open long enough for one passage. Hazel argues, rages, then accepts Jonah's choice; Jonah asks only to be remembered accurately, not kindly. The beat is heartbreak transmuted into trust — love measured by letting someone pay their own price.

chapters.title: Spring Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Hazel. Months later, Hazel reopens the guild under new terms: fair tithes, open books, songs paid forward. When she carves Jonah's name into fresh bone, she hears him answer from the other side, warm and unhurried. The beat is earned hope: inheritance redefined as what we choose to carry on.
